title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to measure the incremental detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator when evaluating LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using the declared model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks (completed_episode_count = 1440). Baseline validator successes = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded pipeline successes = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (shared_initial_generation = 720; repair-stage = 1). The single discordant pair corresponds to pair_id = pair-000504 and maps to the single recorded repair-stage call. Results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20); we report the preregistered design, verified quantitative outcomes, an explanation grounded in validator ceiling effects and task curation, and concise reproducibility pointers to the archived execution bundle (canonical execution manifest).

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow ordering, and policy constraints. A common high-assurance architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to detect runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and prototype reports advocate such layered pipelines but provide limited large-scale paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution. We therefore preregistered and executed a controlled paired study to quantify the downstream (post-generation) detection-rate contribution of an automated sandboxed-emulation stage when the same initial generated candidate is analyzed by both conditions.

Research question and contributions. Preregistered research question: under shared_initial_candidate semantics for synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) a paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with full run accounting; (3) an artifact-grounded explanation for a near-zero marginal effect in this regime and practical boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to matter; (4) reproducible pointers to the canonical archived execution bundle.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centred mitigations. Recent surveys and system reports document that combining LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops is a common practice to raise operational assurance for NetOps artifacts [1]–[3]. These works emphasise that correctness is multidimensional—syntax, sequence/workflow constraints, invariants (for example, keep-one-uplink-up), and dynamic runtime properties often require different V&V primitives. Tool-focused case studies (e.g., evolution of configuration-analysis systems) show improved coverage over time but also persistent gaps for runtime-dependent behaviors that motivate layering emulation after static checks [3].

Empirical patterns and gaps. Prototype integrations of generation with verification report heterogeneous gains: in some task regimes a strong static verifier already catches most dangerous errors, while in others emulation uncovers subtle runtime failures. This literature motivated our paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics so that any observed between-condition discordance can be attributed only to downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations or permitted repair invocations), not to generation variability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Planned Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440) with a minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20 for power planning. Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance (deterministic reseed up to two times for parser failures); irrecoverable technical failures would be handled per the preregistered missingness plan. The study used shared_initial_candidate semantics: exactly one sampled initial candidate was generated per task and reused for both paired conditions.

Task bank, vendors, and topology templates. Confirmatory items were generated deterministically from a task family that encodes explicit intents, required command sequences, allowed-touched fields, and workflow policies (examples: shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). The bank covers three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion checks produced no irrecoverable parser exclusions and a complete_pair_count = 720 in the confirmatory run.

Model and pipeline. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses); recorded model_call accounting shows model_calls_used = 721. Baseline validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (rule-based checks: vendor parsing, command canonicalization, sequence-order checks versus required_command_sequence, workflow constraints, protected-interface invariants, and final-state conformance). Guarded pipeline: baseline validator followed by an automated sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices; emulation observations are mapped to runtime-observation rules that can trigger detections not encoded in the static validator.

Provider-call audit fields and asymmetric counts (requested clarification). The archived provider-call audit records three complementary counts that readers may encounter: (i) total hosted model calls observed (model_calls_used = 721), (ii) stage_counts (counts of provider calls per pipeline stage, e.g., shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1), and (iii) condition_counts whose keys label call attribution to stages that were semantically 'shared' versus 'guarded' during execution (in the archived audit these keys appear as "shared" and "guarded"). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics a single provider call (the shared initial generation) serves both paired conditions; that call is counted in stage_counts as shared_initial_generation and is also attributed in condition_counts to the "shared" category. Additional provider calls that occur only in the guarded-stage repair step are counted in stage_counts as repair and attributed in condition_counts to "guarded." Thus the apparent asymmetry (condition_counts showing 'shared' > 'guarded') is expected and reconciles with episode accounting: 720 shared initial calls plus 1 guarded-only repair call produce the observed model_calls_used = 721. The archived deterministic reconciliation and provider-call audit contain the authoritative per-field values for independent verification.

Analysis. Primary analysis used a paired-binary executor aligned with McNemar-style inference and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Complete-pair handling used the preregistered policy (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs); in this run there were no irrecoverable pairs. Secondary per-class and per-vendor analyses were pre-specified as exploratory with multiplicity adjustments.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and inferential outputs (artifact-grounded). Contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These numeric values are reproduced verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts.

Run accounting and discordant-pair attribution. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation record model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. The unique discordant pair corresponds to pair_id = pair-000504 and maps to the single recorded repair-stage call; auditors can locate that pair_id in the archived execution bundle to inspect the per-episode validator_trace and repair trace. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, this single guarded-only detection is attributable either to a guarded-emulation observation outside the validator rule-set or to the recorded repair invocation.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Representative scoring traces show that most shared_initial candidates complied with the validator (violation_count = 0) and that emulation largely corroborated validator findings in this curated task bank. Difficulty composition (preregistered strata) in the confirmatory set: extreme = 90 (12.5%), hard = 180 (25.0%), medium = 90 (12.5%), very_hard = 360 (50.0%).
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded factors.

1) Validator ceiling and task-rule alignment. The deterministic validator encodes the workflow constraints exercised by the curated tasks; baseline success = 719/720 indicates minimal headroom for emulation to add detections in this regime.

2) Curated inclusion and reduced adversarial exposure. Confirmatory items required parser acceptance and were generated deterministically; this constrained distribution underrepresents runtime-only faults that emulation uncovers in adversarial or uncurated settings.

3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. Reusing the same sampled candidate isolates downstream signals; provider-call accounting shows only a single repair-stage invocation, which matches the single discordant pair. The archived per-episode traces enable auditors to inspect whether the guarded detection followed an emulation observation or a repair-altered candidate.

Operational implications. When operators maintain a high-coverage static validator matched to expected intent patterns and enforce strong prevalidation, an automated sandboxed-emulation stage may provide negligible incremental detection at scale. This is a conditional efficiency boundary, not a universal negative result: in noisy natural-language inputs, adversarial settings, broader multi-vendor diversity, or long-lived stateful procedures, guarded emulation can surface runtime semantics and side-effects that static validators miss.

Recommendations. Based on the archived artifacts we recommend: (i) invest in richer static validators for high-throughput, low-latency pipelines; (ii) deploy guarded sandboxing selectively for high-risk or high-impact changes where emulation fidelity matters; (iii) use adversarial/fuzzing task banks to identify validator gaps and to quantify guarded-stage value in broader regimes.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator to the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation over 720 paired tasks. The guarded pipeline yielded a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call accounting records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair), and the unique discordant pair is pair-000504, which maps to the single repair-stage invocation. We interpret the near-zero marginal effect as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated task design. Generalization to adversarial or production-like regimes requires targeted extensions—adversarial task banks, expanded vendor diversity, multi-validator ensembles, and higher-fidelity emulation—seeded from the archived per-episode traces in the canonical execution bundle.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator create limited ecological diversity and produce a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the archived reconciliation and provider-call audit artifacts.
